messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: High GPU pressure detected in dedicated pool solsticehealth-prod-1 (vpc-12a4). 95% GPU utilization across pool, queueing increased. Paging on-call SRE.

sre_oncall_maya: I'm on it. seeing long tail of large requests, avg queue length 38, 99th latency for token gen ~2.3s. link to metrics: https://graf.redwood/solstice/prod1/gpu

eng_runtime_jihoon: thanks Maya. any pattern on model versions? can we route to a compatible smaller variant while we add capacity?

sre_oncall_maya: traffic mostly to model rwinf-13b-v2 (batching heavy). fallback to rwinf-7b-q4 would drop quality but reduce GPU load by ~45% per request. need ops sign-off for automated fallback.

solutions_ellie: SolsticeHealth CSM here — pinged their oncall for impact details, cc @solstice_oncall_garcia

solstice_oncall_garcia: confirmed from customer side: 3 production endpoints showing 502/504 spikes, some sync jobs timing out. Notified customers' infra team, they asked for ETA on mitigation.

eng_runtime_jihoon: two parallel mitigations proposed: (1) request dedicated burst +4 GPUs for 30m while we stabilize, (2) enable temporary routing to rwinf-7b-q4 for non-critical endpoints. prefer both if possible.

ops_lead_rafa: we can authorize a limited burst. what's the exact command? Also need owner for rollback and cost approval.

sre_oncall_maya: draft command: `/dedicated-burst request --tenant solsticehealth --pool solsticehealth-prod-1 --add-gpus 4 --duration 30m --reason "prod queueing, temporary relief"`

ops_lead_rafa: approved. I authorize up to 4 GPUs for 30m. cost owner: Solutions (Ellie) to confirm with customer for overage.

solutions_ellie: will confirm with Solstice. tagging billing and the account rep. Solstice gave verbal OK for temporary burst to restore SLAs.

infra_bot: Burst request queued: ID brst-171890. Provisioning GPUs in us-west-2, expected ready ~3m.

eng_runtime_jihoon: while burst starts, I'm pushing a low-risk routing change: non-critical endpoints -> rwinf-7b-q4. config snippet:
```
route:
  - path: /ingest/batch -> model: rwinf-7b-q4 (weight 0.4)
  - path: /chat/async -> model: rwinf-13b-v2 (weight 0.6)
```

sre_oncall_maya: applying routing now. will monitor queue and error rate.

infra_bot: Burst brst-171890: GPUs provisioned and joined pool solsticehealth-prod-1. pool available capacity +4.

sre_oncall_maya: immediate drop in queue length to 8, 504s falling. keep monitoring for 10m then reassess.

ops_lead_rafa: handoff plan: Maya will run the mitigation, Jihoon to take follow-up for config and rollout analysis. Handoff to next oncall at 1718903600. Postmortem owner: Rafa. Please log any config changes.

solstice_oncall_garcia: customer reports latency returning to normal on their side. thanks team.

eng_runtime_jihoon: I'll add a temporary KV cache size tweak to reduce memory pressure on the 13b workers: `kv_cache_max_entries=12000 -> 8000` during burst window.

sre_oncall_maya: noted change. monitoring looks stable. planned burst expiration at +30m unless we extend.

solutions_ellie: billing confirmed with customer for emergency burst. they accepted costs for this window.

sre_oncall_maya: closing interim paging thread — will keep this thread updated until postmortem. :white_check_mark:

ops_lead_rafa: good job. remind next oncall to include traffic distribution and model fallback rationale in postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: burst brst-171890 activated, initial impact mitigated. will post final report after postmortem.
summary: Dedicated pool solsticehealth-prod-1 hit high GPU utilization. Team authorized 4-GPU burst and temporary routing to smaller model. Customer impact reduced; billing approved. Postmortem scheduled.
